text:
alex: Heads-up — customer dashboard (insights/9d2f) briefly showed quota bars for org-55 while logged in as org-9 :eyes:
maya: which environment/cluster? can you repro?
alex: console.prod.eu, only seen during the canary window around 08:10 UTC. quick snapshot: https://console.prod/insights/9d2f — looked like the usage bars belonged to a different org id.
chris: hmm, did we change any affinity or header routing last week? :thinking:
maya: we did adjust route affinity to prefer header->cookie->ip fallback. could be a mismatch in the cache key.
alex: captured raw headers from a repro request:
```
GET /api/insights/9d2f
Host: console.prod.eu
X-Org: org-9
Cookie: rdw_affinity=org-55; other=...
```
so header says org-9 but cookie had org-55. backend rendered panels using cookie-bound cache entry.
tess: tagging ops-bot to grab request samples and metric slices @ops-bot :mag:
ops-bot: Collected 120 requests in window 08:08-08:14 UTC. 2.3% had X-Org present but cookie affinity conflicting. Log bundle: s3://redwood-ops/488/4842001111/logs.zip
chris: that explains a transient graph mashup — rendered data came from a cached panel keyed by affinity cookie. not strictly a data leak at storage layer but UI surfaced the wrong cached blob.
maya: quick theory: cache key uses either X-Org or cookie depending on presence, but rendering layer trusts whichever the routing middleware attaches downstream. if header missing sometimes we fall back to cookie; reverse can happen too.
alex: visible impact: a few dashboards showed other org usage for ~30-90s before refresh. customer reported it. want to avoid even that surface-level bleed.
chris: I can sketch a guard: in routing middleware assert that X-Org (if present) matches session.owner if session exists; otherwise refuse to serve cached blobs and force re-render. quick patch would return 409/refresh header for mismatches. anyone object? :+1:
tess: need telemetry too — surface how many users hit cache mismatch and which dashboard ids. I'll add a saved query and an alert. Query: saved/telemetry/affinity-mismatch-2026
maya: also consider binding cache key strictly to a canonical org header we set at the gateway (normalize X-Redwood-Org) and strip legacy rdw_affinity in the console path. prevents old cookies from winning.
alex: can we hotfix routing middleware in canary first? we don't want mass rollbacks.
chris: i'll open a small PR with a middleware guard and a feature flag guarded rollout. PR: https://git.redwood/infr/console/pull/6421 — will deploy to canary cluster first.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-44: "Transient UI affinity mismatch — cross-org quota render". Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-44
tess: rolling a telemetry alert now. will also annotate customer ticket with incident id.
maya: after canary, if green we should also ship a cleanup job to expire stale rdw_affinity cookies (set short ttl) and update gateway to always set X-Redwood-Org.
alex: good plan. chris, can you own the patch? tess, you handle telemetry and customer comms? maya/ops will coordinate cookie prune.
chris: owning patch and canary rollout. posting updates in this thread. :shipit:
tess: telemetry alert created, customer updated, incident linked.
alex: monitoring dashboards now. will post if anything odd shows up. thanks team.
chris: pushed hotfix to canary at 09:02 UTC, flagged behind feature flag ff/affinity-guard.
maya: rolling cookie prune proposal in infra backlog: INFRA-2042.
ops-bot: Canary health check OK at 09:05 UTC, no new mismatch events in 10m window.
alex: closing loop — if canary holds for 1h we roll to prod and push cookie prune next week. I'll update ticket.
